## PHASE 1 · PROMPT, KEY ROTATION & GENERATION
Nodes 1–6. Typed trigger (one item per lead, ≤25) → tag-delimited prompt → key pick → Gemini HTTP → JSON parse.
`2` emits `prompt` (raw) and `prompt_json` (JSON-encoded). The HTTP body uses `{{ $json.prompt_json }}` with NO surrounding quotes.
`3` reads `gemini_api_keys` once (`executeOnce`); `4` picks a key per lead, round-robin, and preserves every lead field.
Untrusted PDF text is wrapped in `<lead_field>` and declared DATA, never instructions.
`5` batches 1 request per 7 s (≈8.5 req/min; each key sees ≈4 with rotation) and is `onError: continueRegularOutput` so a 429 never drops an item — the count must stay at 25 for the index pairing in `7`.

## PHASE 2 · VALIDATE & CREATE DRAFT
Nodes 7–13. Index-paired re-attach of lead identity → content rules → `gmail draft.create`.
A rejected draft is quarantined with a reason code; `done` is written only after Gmail returns an `id`.

## 🔴 MANUAL STEPS (after import)
- **Re-point the parent:** `18 Draft Batch Emails` → pick this workflow. Import mints a NEW workflow id, so the old link breaks.
- **Gmail** (`gmailOAuth2`, scope `gmail.compose`): `9 Create Gmail Draft` — drafts only, no send node exists.
- **Supabase** (`supabaseApi`, secret key): `3 Fetch Gemini Keys`, `5a Update Key Usage`, `10 Mark Rows Drafted`, `12 Mark Rows Failed`.
- **Gemini needs NO n8n credential.** Keys come from the `gemini_api_keys` table (`id`, `api_key`, `daily_usage`, `key_name`). The 19/run-per-key limit is enforced in `4`.
